NutriFresh Foods Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press * then 1 on your telephone keypad if you're using a landline or the Q&A button in the webcast interface if you're online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods Inc.'s Q2 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Growth Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures across key commodities like cocoa and sugar.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: our capital expenditure plans and priorities, pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and full year, market share trends for our major brands, EPS guidance and key assumptions, the impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, and our revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance.

On capital expenditures, we're ramping up investments to build capacity, automate operations, and advance sustainability while targeting strong returns. Pricing and RGM have been pivotal in driving organic growth through layered increases and tech-enabled optimization. For organic sales, we're guiding to mid-single digits ahead. Market share is expanding across core brands in beverages and snacks. EPS outlook is raised on volume strength and productivity. FX has been a headwind but our hedges mitigate it. And overall, we're reaffirming full-year guidance with confidence.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria to provide more detail on our financial results and expand on these areas.

Maria Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q2 2024. Net sales were $4.52 billion, representing a 6.8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.3%, impacted by elevated commodity costs but bolstered by effective pricing and supply chain efficiencies. Operating income was $682 million, and adjusted earnings per share were $1.12, up 8% from last year. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases under our $1.5 billion program.

To give you deeper insight into the strategic areas Alex highlighted, let me expand on each.

Starting with our capital expenditure plans and priorities for FY2024 and beyond. Capex is central to our strategy for margin expansion, supply chain resilience, and growth in segments like plant-based beverages and functional snacks. For FY2024, we're targeting $650 million in total Capex, up 12% from $580 million last year. This disciplined spend aims for over 12% return on invested capital on new projects, with paybacks under three years. The allocation is 35% or $227 million to manufacturing expansion, 30% or $195 million to automation and digital tools, 20% or $130 million to sustainability, and 15% or $98 million to maintenance and supply chain upgrades. This helps counter inflation in cocoa up 25% YoY and sugar up 18%.

On capacity expansion, that $227 million addresses surging demand for health-focused products. In North America, 45% of revenue, $100 million funds two new aseptic filling lines in Modesto, California, boosting NutriFresh PlantPower almond and oat milks by 25% to tap the $15 billion U.S. plant-based market where we hold 7.2% share per Nielsen. This de-risks against California's almond yield drops of 15% from drought. In APAC, up 12% for us, $75 million builds a greenfield plant in Ho Chi Minh City for functional teas and electrolyte waters, localizing 60% production amid 20% U.S.-China tariffs and riding an 8% CAGR in non-alc beverages. EMEA gets $52 million for FiberCrunch bar upgrades in the Netherlands, amid Europe's 10% premium snacking surge.

Automation and digital transformation at $195 million tackles labor shortages and 6% wage inflation. $80 million for robotic palletizers and AI fillers in 12 North American plants aims to lift OEE to 92% from 85%, adding 150 bps to margins, similar to Coca-Cola's efforts. $60 million enhances our Enterprise AI with SAP for demand forecasting, cutting stockouts 30% and inventory 18% in beverages, like Nestlé's yield tools. In LATAM, $35 million adds blockchain to Guadalajara for avocado smoothies.

Sustainability investments of $130 million build on 22% emissions cuts since 2021 toward net-zero by 2040. $50 million for solar and heat pumps at five U.S. plants covers 40% energy needs, saving $15 million yearly like Danone. $40 million shifts 70% of bottles to rPET, cutting virgin resin 25% amid EU and U.S. regs. $25 million for water recycling in India hits 80% at Mumbai.

Maintenance and supply chain at $98 million sustains 95% on-time delivery, with $40 million for cold chain in Texas and Ontario against avian flu egg cost spikes of 40%. FY2025 Capex rises to $700 million, heavier in APAC and digital twins, targeting 15% ROIC and 14% EBIT margins by 2026 in the $4.5 trillion F&B space.

Next, our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, core to top-line resilience amid 15-20% YoY commodity rises per Rabobank. Net revenue hit $4.2 billion, up 6.8%, with organic at 5.2%, beating CPG's 3.1% IRI average. Price/mix drove +4.1 points, volume +0.1, trade spend -0.2.

Pricing was layered: 5.2% average hikes since Q1, 4-6% on NA snacks/beverages in Q2, 3-5% on dairy/plant-based in EMEA/APAC Q3. Net price per unit up 4.3%, elasticity -2.3 better than peers. Beverages elasticity -3.1 saw 1.2% volume dip offset by 6.8% premium uplift on HydraBoost, up 12% at Walmart/Kroger. Promos down to 18% off, shifting spend to base prices for 220 bps net price per kilo gain. Snacks grew 5.6% organically despite flat category.

Our RevOptix AI platform on IRI/SPINS data drives RGM: SKU rationalization to 950 from 1,200, mega-packs now 28% volume for +1.2 mix points; promo ROI up via causal models, cutting BOGOs 30% for 60 bps growth; premium now 35% revenue, e-com 12% up 22%.

Regionally: NA +7.2% on 5.8% pricing; EMEA +3.9% premium dairy up 11%; APAC/LATAM +4.8% on localized packs. Ahead, 3-5% Q4 pricing for +4% FY organic, $150M RevOptix 2.0, premium target 15% by 2025. Gross margin up 210 bps.

Turning to organic sales growth guidance for Q4 and FY2025: mid-single digits at 4-5% Q4, 4-6% FY2025, building on Q3's 4.2%. Pricing 2-3 points, volume/mix 1.5-2.5. Beverages 5-7% on VitaGlow/Hydrate+ share +12% IRI, 85% c-store ACV. Snacks 3-5% on protein bars +15% velocity for GLP-1 trends. Convenience 4-6% on meal kits.

NA 4.5-5.5%, EMEA 3-5% sustainable packaging; APAC 6-8% China/India; LatAm 2-4%. Underpinned by 12 Q4 SKUs for $200M FY25 sales, digital shelf +25% online, $150M productivity. Risks: frugality, weather; upsides: inflation cooldown. Targets 150-200 bps margin expansion.

On market share trends for major brands, per Nielsen/IRI through July: +110 bps aggregate to 24.7% in beverages/snacks. Zest Cola +1.8 to 31.2% in CSD vs. Coke's -0.9, on zero-sugar reformulation, 92% ACV. Functional like VitalQuench +3.2 to 18.5%, #2 enhanced water. CrunchBites +4.5 to 11% alt-protein snacks.

NA +140 bps to 29.1%; Europe +80 bps to 19.4% on localized Zest; APAC +210 bps to 15.2% VitalQuench #3 China; LatAm +90 bps Zest 28% Mexico. Thrive25 $750M fermentation cuts COGS 8%; AI trade opt 20% ROI; recycled PET +NPS. Tailwinds: 15-20% premium category CAGR.

For EPS guidance and key assumptions: Raising FY2024 adjusted EPS to $4.65-$4.85, 8-12% over $4.28, on 6-8% organic revenue (NA 7-9%, EMEA 5-7%, APAC 4-6%, LatAm flat-2%). Gross margin +120-150 bps to 37.5-38% via Supply Chain 2.0 $250M, hedges. OpEx +5-6%, margin 14.5-15%. Tax 24%. Pillars: wellness 15 SKUs, regen ag, divestitures +20 bps FY25 EPS. Risks: geopolitics, labor 4%.

Regarding impact of foreign exchange rates: Q2 reported +2.1% to $2.48B, constant currency +5.4%; YTD +1.8% vs. +6.2%, $420M drag or 4.4 points. LatAm -7.2 pts Brazil real -18%; EMEA -4.1 euro -9%; APAC -1.8. NA neutral. Hedging 75% 2024 exposures, 65% local sourcing. Localization $250M plants India/Poland. Q4 drag 2-3 pts, CC 5-7%.

Finally, on full-year guidance: Reaffirming consolidated net revenues $14.8-$15.0B, 4-5% reported/3-4% organic; adjusted EPS $4.25-$4.35, 6-9% growth; EBITDA margin +50-100 bps to 18-18.5% via $250M VitaEfficiency. Beverages 5-6%, Snacks 2-3%, Health 8-10%. NA 5%, APAC/LatAm 9%, EMEA 1%. Shaping: $300M divestitures, SAP rollout, green bonds. Risks: FX, inflation; positioned via +7% pricing, $300M savings.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance across these lines.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation in commodities like cocoa and dairy remains elevated at 12-20% YoY, but our layered pricing up 5.2% and productivity from Supply Chain 2.0 have more than offset it, delivering gross margin expansion. We're hedged on 70% of key inputs and focused on premium mix for resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact?

Jordan Lee (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. We're launching 12 SKUs in Q4, including keto snacks and zero-sugar functionals, targeting $200M incremental FY25 sales. Early pilots show 15% velocity lifts in protein bars and hydration, driving 1-2 points to organic growth via wellness trends.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Taylor Kim (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, we're diversifying with 65% local-for-local sourcing, blockchain traceability, and $98M in cold chain hardening. AI forecasting cut waste 12%, maintaining 95% on-time delivery despite avian flu and weather, while new plants in Vietnam/Netherlands add redundancy.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Patel (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Maria Chen (CFO):
Emily, we're confident in mid-single-digit organic growth for H2, with Q4 at 4-5%, driven by pricing discipline, innovation velocity, and margin gains. FX headwinds moderate, and productivity supports EPS at the high end of our raised guide, positioning for FY25 compounding.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriFresh Foods Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
